hero.audience_line: For parents of babies, toddlers and preschoolers, new moms and dads, expectant parents, grandparents and godparents, and the Sunday school, nursery and preschool teachers who read to little ones.
hero.tagline: Before your child can read a word, they can know whose they are. Twenty-one watercolor “I am” affirmations, each with a Father’s Heart Bible verse and a simple prayer, for parents to read aloud with children ages 0 to 5.

audience.headline: A mom in South Africa wrote a book that answers one question for the littlest listener: who am I?
audience.body: For parents of babies, toddlers and preschoolers, new moms and dads, expectant parents, grandparents and godparents, and the Sunday school, nursery and preschool teachers who read to little ones, and Christian families who want a child to grow up knowing they are loved, chosen and never alone. Who Am I? is a devotional for parents to read aloud over and with their little ones, not a book a child reads alone. Each of its twenty-one pages pairs one “I am” truth with a verse from the Father’s Heart Bible, a few short sentences a young child can take in, and a one-line prayer of thanks. The pattern never changes, so even the youngest listener learns what comes next, and the closing page gathers every affirmation into one answer. A note on content: the prayers are simple thank-you prayers. One, on the “I am forgiven” page, thanks Jesus for taking our punishment on the cross, and the “I am healed” page speaks of our Father helping a child feel better, inside and out.

quote.text: “I am who my Father says I am.”

what_makes.title: What makes this book for little ones and the people who read to them
paras: It opens with a page headed Things my heavenly Father says about me, and every page after it keeps the same gentle order: the affirmation, the verse, a short explanation and a prayer. Little ones learn by hearing the same words many times, and the book is built for exactly that kind of repetition.
Five things set it apart:
list: It is a repeat affirmation book. Twenty-one short “I am” declarations, made to be read again and again until a child knows them by heart.
Every truth rests on Scripture. Each page quotes the Father’s Heart Bible, from Psalm 139 and Jeremiah 31 to Romans 8 and Matthew 5.
The words fit a small child. Each explanation is one or two short sentences, such as “My heavenly Father makes my heart new.”
Each page ends with a prayer a parent and child can say together, most of them beginning “Thank you, heavenly Father.”
It closes with a declaration. The last spread asks So who am I? and answers with all twenty-one truths and one joyful line: That is who I am!

sections.h2: For parents of babies, toddlers and preschoolers
paras: You do not have to wait until your child can read. The book is made to be read over a baby and with a toddler, at bedtime, at naptime or in any quiet moment, one affirmation at a time or the whole book in one sitting. Because the pattern never changes, children soon begin to say the words along with you.

sections.h2: For grandparents, godparents and expectant parents
paras: It is a gift for new and growing families: a square 8.5 x 8.5 book with soft watercolor illustrations, easy to hold with a little one on your lap. It suits a new baby, a baby dedication, or any family that wants a child to hear our Father’s truth from the very first years of life.

sections.h2: For Sunday school, nursery and preschool teachers
paras: Each page is short enough to read to a group and simple enough for a preschooler to echo back. The twenty-one verses give children’s ministry leaders a ready list of Bible verses for kids, each with a sentence that explains it and a one-line prayer.

Pages such as I have a family, I am chosen and I am never alone speak directly to belonging. The book says it plainly: “I belong to the family of God. He is my heavenly Father and He loves me as His very own child.”

paras: The sixth affirmation is for the moments a little one feels afraid. It rests on Hebrews 13:5:
“I will never leave you, never abandon you.”

The explanation is two sentences: “Even when I feel scared, my heavenly Father is always with me. He promises to never leave my side.” The prayer thanks Him that “I never have to feel alone because I know you are with me.”
The seventh page gives a child courage from Joshua 1:9:
“Be strong and courageous. Do not fear or be discouraged, for I, your Father, am with you wherever you go.”
It explains: “My heavenly Father gives me courage when I feel afraid. His strength lives inside me and helps me be brave.”

The last spread asks the question in the title and answers it with every truth in the book, read straight through: I am wonderfully made. I am a child of my heavenly Father. I am loved. I belong to Jesus. And on, all the way to I am blessed. I am victorious. It ends with one line for the child to say:
“That is who I am!”

author.bio: Karen Inge Hailstones is a Christian wife and mother of three from KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. She grew up on a sugar cane farm near Wartburg. She wrote Who Am I? so even the littlest ones can hear who our Father says they are, and grow up knowing their identity in Christ.

why.title: Why this book exists
paras: Karen wrote it for the youngest children, the ones who cannot read yet. Her About the Author page says the book grew from her desire to share the love of our Father in its simplest form:
“So even the littlest ones can hear who He says they are.”
The back cover says what she hopes every child will answer when they are asked who they are:
“I am who my Father says I am.”

faq.q: What is Who Am I? about?
faq.a: It is a read-aloud devotional by Karen Inge Hailstones that answers the question in its title for very young children. Twenty-one “I am” affirmations show a child who they are in our Father’s eyes, each with a Father’s Heart Bible verse, a short explanation and a prayer. The closing page gathers them all into one answer: That is who I am!

faq.q: What age is Who Am I? for?
faq.a: Ages 0 to 5: babies from birth, toddlers, preschoolers and children who are just learning to read. It is written for a parent, grandparent or teacher to read aloud over and with the child, not for a child to read alone.

faq.q: What are the 21 “I am” affirmations in the book?
faq.a: They are, in order: I am wonderfully made; I am a child of my heavenly Father; I am loved; I belong to Jesus; I am chosen; I am never alone; I am brave and strong; I am Father's treasure; I am forgiven; I am a new creation; I have a family; I am protected; I am gifted; I have a purpose; I am healed; I am free; I am more than a conqueror; I am the light of the world; I am safe and calm; I am blessed; and I am victorious.

faq.q: Which Bible verses for kids are in Who Am I?
faq.a: They are, in order: Psalm 139:14; 1 John 3:1; Jeremiah 31:3; John 10:14; Ephesians 1:4; Hebrews 13:5; Joshua 1:9; Deuteronomy 7:6; 1 John 1:9; Ezekiel 36:26; John 1:12; Psalm 91:11; 1 Peter 4:10; Jeremiah 29:11; Isaiah 53:5; John 8:36; Romans 8:37; Matthew 5:14; John 14:27; Ephesians 1:3; and 1 Corinthians 15:57. Every verse is quoted from the Father’s Heart Bible, one on each affirmation page.

faq.q: Does it teach a child their identity in Christ?
faq.a: Yes. That is the whole aim of the book. Pages such as I belong to Jesus, I am a new creation and I have a family tell a child who they are because of our Father’s love, and the author wrote it so children can grow up knowing their identity in Christ.

faq.q: Is it a good book to show a child that God loves them?
faq.a: Yes. The third affirmation is I am loved, from Jeremiah 31:3: “I have loved you with everlasting love.” It explains that before the child was even born, their heavenly Father already loved them, and that His love will never run out and never end.

faq.q: Can it help a child’s self-esteem and courage?
faq.a: The back cover says it builds a child’s self-esteem on who our Father says they are. Affirmations like I am Father’s treasure, I am brave and strong and I am more than a conqueror are written to be repeated until the child knows them by heart.

faq.q: Is Who Am I? a board book?
faq.a: No. It is printed as a paperback and as a hardback, both 8.5 x 8.5 inches with 50 full-color pages, and as an eBook. The square size makes it easy to hold with a little one on your lap.

faq.q: Is it a good bedtime book?
faq.a: Yes. It is made for laps, bedtimes and quiet moments. You can read one affirmation and its prayer at bedtime or the whole book in one sitting, and because the pattern never changes, children soon say the words along with you.

faq.q: Can preschoolers use it for scripture memory?
faq.a: Yes. Each affirmation is short enough for a toddler to remember and each prayer is simple enough for a preschooler to echo back. Over weeks and months of reading, the twenty-one truths move from the page into a child’s heart, and the closing page becomes a declaration they can speak on their own.

hero.audience_line: For believers who are worn out from performing for approval, who carry an orphan heart or a father wound, and who want to rest in being our Father’s beloved child.
hero.tagline: Hear your Heavenly Father speak in His own words from Scripture, and learn to live as His beloved child instead of an orphan in heart.

audience.headline: Every soul is asking one question: Who am I? This short book lets our Father answer it in His own words.
audience.body: For Christians who know Jesus as Savior but still live like orphans in heart, for anyone whose earthly father was absent, harsh, demanding or silent, and for anyone tired of measuring their worth by results. Kevin White gathers the Father’s words from Scripture and arranges them in His voice, so you can hear Him speak directly to you, then answer with declarations you speak out loud. A note on subjects: the book is warm and direct, and it is written for adults. It names the fear of abandonment and touches on abuse, neglect and emotional distance. Its statement of faith is plainly charismatic: it welcomes prophecy, healing, tongues and deliverance, and it defines marriage as a covenant between one man and one woman. It is a short devotional and confession book, not a study Bible or a commentary.

quote.text: “Sons and daughters on paper, but orphans in heart.”

what_makes.title: What makes this book different
paras: The book does not explain our Father from a distance. It lets Him speak. As the author puts it in How to Read This Book: “We have not put words in God’s mouth. He has already spoken.” The passages have been gathered and arranged so that you hear Him speak to you directly.
Five things set it apart:
list: It is written in the Father’s voice. Eighteen short sections in Part Two, from Who Do You Say That I Am? to My Answer, speak to you as “beloved.”
Every section ends with My Confession, a short list of declarations to say out loud, because faith comes by hearing.
Where the Father’s Heart Bible rendering reveals something a standard translation does not, the New Living Translation and the FHB appear side by side so you can hear the difference.
It includes a full statement of faith that makes the Father’s heart central, from the Scriptures and the Trinity to the return of Christ.
It is short on purpose. It is an Express Book of 96 pages, “intentionally written and designed to be read in under an hour.”

sections.h2: For believers who feel like orphans in heart
paras: The introduction describes many faithful churchgoers this way: they know Jesus as Savior, but they have not followed Him home to the Father. “They can serve a Master. They cannot rest in a Father.” If you read about the Father’s love but cannot feel it, the book was written for you.

sections.h2: For anyone carrying a father wound
paras: In the section on marriage and family, our Father speaks to those whose earthly father was absent, harsh, demanding or silent, and who learned to perform for love or gave up believing love was possible. His answer is plain: “I am the Father your earthly father could never fully be.”

sections.h2: For people worn out from performing
paras: “Our whole culture runs on results. Perform. Produce. Prove yourself.” The book answers that pressure with identity before activity: you are loved first, and you serve from that love instead of working to earn it.

The Express Books page at the front of the book calls it a needed resource for every company, church or team, affordably priced for easy sharing, with bulk copies available. Each section is short enough to read and confess together in one sitting.

stories.h2: What the Father did at the Fall
paras: The Wound We All Carry asks the reader to look at the garden again. “We have been taught to read the story of the garden as punishment.” But what did our Father do even as He sent Adam and Eve out? He clothed them. Genesis 3:21 appears in both the New Living Translation and the Father’s Heart Bible, and the book draws the line plainly:
“The Fall was not the Father abandoning His children.”

In the section My Son, our Father points to the baptism of Jesus. Before Jesus performed a single miracle or preached a single sermon, the Father spoke: “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.” The book calls this the pattern for every believer:
“I was establishing His identity before His activity.”

stories.h2: A seat at the King’s table
paras: Living in the Father’s Heart retells the story of Mephibosheth, broken and convinced he had no claim to the King’s favor, until David told him he would eat at the king’s table. The book turns that into an invitation to daily communion with our Father:
“The bread is broken. The cup is poured. Your seat is reserved.”

author.name: Kevin White

Married to his high school sweetheart, Shelly, for nearly forty years, he and Shelly lead Spirit Media, Father’s Heart Bible™ and Work On Yourself, empowering Kingdom Messengers. Kevin and Shelly live in North Carolina with their family.

why.title: Why this book exists
paras: The introduction starts with a phrase from Jesus: “No one can come to the Father except through Me.” For centuries, the book says, the church has heard “way to heaven,” but He said “way to the Father.”
“Millions have believed in the way but missed the destination.”
Before You Begin names what has been missing. The historic confessions declared that God is Father, but they rarely made the Father’s heart central:
“They told us what we are saved from—but not fully to whom we are saved.”

faq.q: What is Father’s Heart - Beloved Identity about?
faq.a: It is a short book by Kevin White that gathers our Father’s words from Scripture and arranges them in His voice, so you can hear Him tell you who you are: His beloved child. Each section ends with My Confession, declarations you speak out loud. It closes with a statement of faith and daily affirmations.

faq.q: Does the book talk about the fear of abandonment?
faq.a: Yes. The Wound We All Carry calls the fear of abandonment the deepest wound in human history, one that began when Adam and Eve hid in the garden. It says the world gives that wound many names, including anxiety, codependency, rejection and trust issues, and answers it with Jesus’ words on the cross and Romans 8:15. It is a devotional book, not a clinical guide.

In the book it is the condition of believers who are “sons and daughters on paper, but orphans in heart”: they can serve a Master but cannot rest in a Father. In the section My Spirit, our Father says, “Allow My love to consume and dissolve the orphan spirit.”

faq.q: What does the book say about the spirit of adoption?
faq.a: It quotes Romans 8:15: you did not receive a spirit that makes you fearful slaves, but our Father’s Spirit when He adopted you as His own children, so now we call Him “Abba, Father.” The book teaches that the first work of the Spirit is to establish that identity: “Before power, identity.”

faq.q: What are the Bible confessions in this book?
faq.a: Every section in Part Two ends with My Confession, a short list of first-person statements drawn from what our Father has just said, such as “I am a beloved child of God, and my Father is well pleased with me.” The book asks you to speak them out loud, because faith comes by hearing.

faq.q: What are the daily affirmations of faith and identity?
faq.a: They are, in order: I Was Chosen Before I Performed; I Am a Beloved Child, Not an Orphan; My Father Is Well Pleased With Me; I Live From Identity, Not For It; and My Father Works In Me Before Through Me. The book asks you to repeat them slowly each morning, out loud.

faq.q: Does the book include a statement of faith?
faq.a: Yes. Part Three opens with a full statement of faith that makes the Father’s heart central. It covers the Scriptures, the Trinity, God the Father, Jesus Christ, the Holy Spirit, the Fall, salvation, baptism and communion, formation, restoration, mission, the spiritual realm, the Church, marriage and family, and the return of Christ.

faq.q: What does it say about intimacy with God?
faq.a: In My Heart for You, our Father says He is pursuing you for three things. They are, in order: intimacy; identity; and inheritance. Intimacy means being close to Him, “not as a servant knows a master, but as a child knows a father.”

faq.q: Why are two Bible translations shown side by side?
faq.a: The book is a forerunner to the Father’s Heart Bible. Where the FHB rendering reveals something the New Living Translation does not, both appear together so you can hear the difference for yourself. When there is no meaningful difference, only the FHB is shown.
